item.title: The digital you
item.description:
Niloy is a cheerful and friendly student, yet some of his classmates always seemed to avoid him. He never understood why.
One semester, they were assigned a group project together. As they worked closely, his teammates realized that Niloy was kind, helpful, and easy to get along with.
Curious, Niloy asked, “Why did you avoid me before?”
Their answer surprised him.
“We followed you on social media,” they said. “Your posts and comments made you seem arrogant and rude. But after getting to know you, we realized you're actually a very nice person.”
That was a wakeup call for Niloy. He learned that before people meet us in real life, they often meet our digital identity first.
Social media is more than a place to share photos and updates. It is a reflection of how you present yourself to the world. Your posts, comments, and online behaviour help others form an impression of your personality.
Today, many employers review candidates’ social media profiles before making hiring decisions. In some cases, even official institutions may consider online behaviour as part of professional or administrative evaluation processes.
Whether we realize it or not, our digital footprint speaks on our behalf long before we meet people in person.
Building a positive digital identity
Building a positive digital identity requires conscious effort. Before posting anything online, ask yourself whether it is kind, true, and necessary. Be mindful of your tone, communicate respectfully, even when you disagree with others. Think carefully before reacting to any controversial content.
Respect copyright rules. If you share someone else's writing, ideas, photos, or other content, make sure to acknowledge the original creator and give proper credit.
Protect both your own privacy and the privacy of others. Follow accounts that inspire learning and personal growth rather than those that spread negativity. Use social media to showcase your skills, achievements, and values in a humble and professional way.
Avoid comparing your life to others’ highlight reels and remember that your worth is not measured by likes or followers. Every post, comment, and interaction contributes to your digital footprint, so strive to create content that adds value, supports others and leaves a positive digital legacy.
The need for early Digital Education
Several countries are tightening regulations on social media use among minors due to growing concerns about digital safety, mental health, and online behaviour.
However, restrictions alone are not enough. Young people also need guidance on how to use social media wisely and responsibly. By learning digital etiquette, critical thinking and online safety from an early age students can build a positive digital footprint and develop healthy online habits.
Social Media and Professional Responsibility
As students grow into professionals, responsible social media use becomes even more important. In professional environments, online behaviour can affect not only an individual's reputation but also the image of the organization they represent.
For example, a recent directive from the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE) advised government primary school teachers to follow social media guidelines and avoid sharing content that negatively portrays the education system, government institutions or official policies.
This highlights a key soft skill in the digital age: Responsible online communication. Knowing what to share, where to share it, and how to express concerns responsibly is an essential part of digital professionalism.
AI and Responsible Use of Social Media
When using AI on social media, responsibility is essential. People should avoid creating or sharing misleading, irrelevant, or harmful AI-generated content online.
I once saw a post about an air force pilot who died in a plane crash. After the incident, someone created an AI-generated video showing the pilot waving and walking near the crashed aircraft while his grieving parents and wife were shown crying. The video was deeply disturbing and disrespectful.
We must consider the emotional impact of such content. Imagine how the family would feel if they saw a fabricated video about their loved one. It can cause deep pain and trauma.
Today, AI-generated misinformation and manipulated content are spreading rapidly on social media. This is why we must remain careful and responsible before creating, sharing or believing anything online.
Be Smart. Be Safe. Be Positive
Social media is a powerful tool. Use it wisely to learn, connect, grow, and make a positive impact on yourself and the world.
Remember, your digital identity is your invisible voice. Make sure it speaks with kindness, responsibility and respect.
Tanzila Taher Toma is a soft skills educator.

Gold prices cut again a day after hike
item.description:
Gold prices in Bangladesh have been cut again, just a day after the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) raised them.
The new prices took effect from 10am Friday, following a decline in the price of refined or pure gold.
The price of 22-carat hallmarked gold has been set at Tk20,115 per gram, down Tk185 from Tk20,300. This means a reduction of around Tk2,158 per bhori (11.664 grams).
Including VAT, the price of one bhori of 22-carat gold jewellery has fallen from Tk236,779 to Tk234,621.
The new rates were set at a meeting of BAJUS’s Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Friday morning, considering the decline in refined gold prices and the overall market situation.
Compared with Thursday, 21-carat gold has fallen by Tk180 per gram, 18-carat by Tk155 and traditional gold by Tk125.

Tanzid landmark century, Shanto fifty give Bangladesh 88-run lead at Tea against Australia
item.description:
Bangladesh strengthened its commanding position against Australia as Tanzid Hasan Tamim struck a historic maiden Test century and Najmul Hossain Shanto continued his fluent innings to take the visitors to 286-3 at Tea on the second day of the first Test on Friday.
Bangladesh now lead by 88 runs with seven wickets in hand, having added 105 runs in 27 overs during the second session. The visitors have dominated all five sessions of the Test so far after Hasan Mahmud’s career-best 6-55 helped dismiss Australia for 198 on the opening day.
Tanzid, playing only his second Test, completed a memorable century from 188 balls before eventually falling for 101 off 197 deliveries, with eight fours and a six.
His hundred made him the first Bangladesh batter to score a Test century in Australia, surpassing Hannan Sarkar’s previous record of 76 at Cairns in 2003.
The left-hander showed remarkable patience after being given an early reprieve, with Nathan Lyon dropping a chance when he was yet to score. He later survived another opportunity when Steve Smith failed to hold a sharp edge at first slip.
Tanzid eventually fell to Lyon, attempting to hit the spinner down the ground but picking out Starc at long-off. His dismissal ended a superb innings but did little to halt Bangladesh’s momentum.
Shanto took charge after Tanzid’s departure, reaching 79 not out from 114 balls, including seven fours and a six. He has played with increasing freedom as Australia struggled to find a breakthrough, particularly against Lyon and Josh Hazlewood.
Mushfiqur Rahim also settled quickly, remaining unbeaten on 26 from 35 balls with four boundaries.
The pair added an unbeaten 50-run partnership by tea, ensuring Bangladesh retained control after Tanzid’s departure.
Australia used eight bowlers during the innings, with Lyon bearing the heaviest workload. The veteran spinner had figures of 1-80 from 18 overs at tea as Bangladesh’s batters repeatedly rotated the strike and punished loose deliveries.
Bangladesh had resumed the day on 96-1, with Tanzid and Mominul Haque adding 102 for the second wicket. Mominul narrowly missed a half-century, falling for 49 to Hazlewood.
With the new ball due in two overs after tea, Australia face a crucial passage if they are to find a way back into the contest.
For now, however, Bangladesh are firmly in command, 88 runs ahead and with seven wickets still in hand.
After Hasan Mahmud’s demolition of Australia’s batting, Tanzid’s historic hundred and Shanto’s unbeaten 79 have given Bangladesh a commanding platform to push for a substantial first-innings lead.

New study sheds light on breast cancer treatment resistance
item.description:
Researchers in Australia have discovered why breast cancer treatment stops working for some patients, uncovering an unexpected role of a key cancer-fighting protein.
The study, published in Nature, found that the retinoblastoma (Rb) protein, long viewed as a natural brake on cancer growth, can unexpectedly activate genes that respond to the hormone estrogen. Some of these genes can help cancer cells withstand treatment and retain the ability to regrow, according to a statement released Thursday by Australia's Peter MacCallum Cancer Center.
The research team found that Rb does more than switch off genes that drive cell division. It can also "switch on biological programs that partially work against its own protective effects," said Peter Mac Associate Professor Shom Goel, the study's senior author.
The findings help explain why medicines known as CDK4/6 inhibitors work particularly well with endocrine therapy in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, the most common subtype.
"The CDK4/6 inhibitor activates Rb to stop cancer cells dividing, while endocrine therapy blocks the unwanted estrogen-driven signals that Rb can also trigger. Together, they allow the tumor-suppressing effects of Rb to dominate," Goel said.
However, when cancers become resistant to endocrine therapy, the estrogen-related gene program continues despite treatment, reducing the effectiveness of CDK4/6 inhibitors, researchers found.
"Understanding this previously unknown role of Rb gives us an important new way to think about drug resistance," Goel said, adding the discovery could guide new combination therapies that keep these treatments working for longer and improve outcomes for breast cancer patients.

item.title: 5 arrested for running online betting, gambling ring
item.description:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested five members of an organised ring allegedly involved in operating online betting and gambling platforms.
The arrested suspects are: Rafiqul Islam, 46, Md Sohel, 37, Md Shafiqul Islam, 27, Md Rubel Molla, 33, and Ayub Hossain Ripon, 48. All are from Narsingdi.
The CID’s Cyber Police Centre (CPC) arrested them in separate raids across Narsingdi between Wednesday evening and Thursday.
Police recovered nine mobile phones, 20 SIM cards, cheque books from several banks and other evidence from their possession.
Jasim Uddin Khan, special superintendent of police (media) at the CID, said preliminary questioning indicated the suspects’ links to an organised online betting and gambling network.
“Initial investigations suggest that an organised group operating both in Bangladesh and abroad has been running online betting and gambling websites under various names for a long time,” he said.
The group allegedly arranged betting and gambling for money around international cricket, football and other sporting events, while promoting the activities through social media and other online platforms, Jasim Uddin Khan said.
The CID urged the public to refrain from online gambling and betting activities.

item.title: DMP takes zero-tolerance stance on drugs, snatching
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has directed police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach to drug-related crimes, take effective measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres, and maintain round-the-clock surveillance in snatching-prone areas.
He gave the directives at the monthly crime review meeting for July 2026, held at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium in Rajarbagh in the capital on Thursday. The DMP commissioner instructed police to strengthen intelligence activities alongside regular drives against drug dealers and others involved in drug-related crimes.
He also directed officials concerned to take necessary measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres within their respective police station areas. “If information about such activities is received, immediate legal action should be taken while maintaining regular surveillance,” he said.
To prevent snatching, Mosleh Uddin instructed the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit and Detective Branch (DB) to maintain round-the-clock field presence in coordination with the Crime Division after identifying snatching-prone areas.
He also ordered stronger intelligence surveillance, patrols and operations in those areas and directed the units concerned to work in coordination to bring the criminals to justice.
The DMP chief further asked the officers-in-charge of the relevant police stations and senior officials of the Crime Division to visit the scene of every crime. He stressed the importance of visiting crime scenes in person, collecting necessary evidence and properly examining the circumstances surrounding incidents to establish the facts and make investigations more effective.
Mosleh Uddin also directed field-level police officials to discharge their duties with the highest professionalism, responsibility and dedication to control crime and ensure the safety of city residents.

item.title: JMB member arrested in Savar sent to court
item.description:
Police sent an alleged member of banned militant outfit JMB to court on Thursday, seeking a 10-day remand in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
The accused, identified as Mohammad Arif, 26, was arrested by members of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit from Hemayetpur in Savar on Tuesday. He was produced before the court from Savar Model Police Station around noon on Thursday.
According to police, several bombs were recovered from a bag in Arif’s possession at the time of his arrest. Later, based on information provided by him, police raided his rented residence in South Shyampur, Hemayetpur.
During the raid, police recovered several powerful bombs, cocktails and a large quantity of materials allegedly used to make explosives.
Police subsequently filed a case at Savar Model Police Station under the Anti-Terrorism Act, naming six people, including Arif, and several unidentified others as accused.
According to the case statement, the accused are members of the banned New JMB and had gathered in the Savar area with explosives to carry out acts of sabotage.
The statement also alleged that they supported the ideology of the banned organisation and were involved in activities aimed at creating public panic, threatening public safety and national sovereignty, and attempting to attack law enforcement personnel.
The other named accused are currently absconding, police said.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Alam said Arif was sent to court with a 10-day remand plea.

item.title: Fakhrul’s presidential nomination sparks celebrations in Thakurgaon
item.description:
Thakurgaon, the birthplace of BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, erupted in celebration after reports that he had been finalized as the party’s candidate for Bangladesh’s 23rd presidential election.
Following a high-level BNP meeting on Thursday, news of Fakhrul’s nomination quickly spread across the district. Party activists and local residents gathered at the BNP office and his ancestral home in Kalibari. Supporters organized celebratory processions, distributed sweets and exchanged greetings, turning parts of the town into a festive scene.
Fakhrul became involved in politics as a student at Dhaka University. He later worked as a college teacher before entering local politics and being elected chairman of Thakurgaon Municipality. He subsequently served as a member of parliament, state minister and full minister.
Over more than a decade of political turbulence, Fakhrul played a significant role in keeping the BNP organized and united. His political career also included periods of imprisonment amid the party’s prolonged political struggles.
Residents described his nomination as a major achievement not only for Thakurgaon but also for the wider northern region.
Prof Abu Bakar Siddique, former principal of Thakurgaon Government Women’s College, described Fakhrul as one of the region’s most distinguished figures. He expressed hope that development initiatives for Thakurgaon would receive greater momentum if Fakhrul assumes the presidency.
Dr ABM Khairul Kabir, president of the Thakurgaon chapter of the Bangladesh Medical Association and a former director of Dinajpur Medical College Hospital, said Fakhrul’s achievement was a source of pride for the entire northern region.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the family was deeply moved, calling the nomination recognition of Fakhrul’s lifelong sacrifice, dedication and integrity.
Residents expressed hope that, if elected president, Fakhrul would strengthen democratic institutions and help reflect the hopes and aspirations of ordinary citizens.

item.title: CUET declares campus ponds, ditches hazardous after 3 student drownings
item.description:
Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) has declared all campus ponds and ditches hazardous and banned students from bathing or swimming in them following the drowning of three students.
The directive was issued in a notice signed by Professor Saiful Islam, director of the Directorate of Students’ Welfare, on Thursday.
The notice said all campus ponds had been declared hazardous in the interest of students’ safety. Until further notice, entering, swimming or otherwise going into any campus pond is strictly prohibited.
Violators will be considered to have breached university discipline and face disciplinary action under the university’s rules, the notice said.
CUET currently has two ponds and several ditches on its campus. The decision came after three students drowned in one of the ponds in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, second-year students Chomok Dutta of the Computer Science and Engineering Department and Shanto Deb of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department drowned while bathing in the pond.
Earlier, on July 28, fourth-year Mechanical Engineering student Arnab Saha drowned in the same pond.
According to CUET sources, Shanto and Arnab had entered the pond beside Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall to bathe with friends. They were submerged at one point and later rescued and taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
The latest deaths occurred just two weeks after Arnab’s drowning, leaving the university community in mourning once again.

item.title: Fertilizer sales irregularities grip Rajshahi, farmers protest
item.description:
Farmers across the Rajshahi region are struggling to buy subsidised fertiliser at government-fixed prices, amid allegations of hoarding, diversion and an organised syndicate involving dealers and unauthorised retailers.
The crisis comes as Aman planting is underway, raising concerns among farmers that delays in getting fertiliser could affect crop yields.
Farmers allege that some dealers sell fertiliser allocation orders to black-market traders even before receiving supplies. Others reportedly sell fertiliser directly to retailers from warehouses instead of distributing it through designated outlets. There are also allegations that fertiliser allocated to one district or upazila is being diverted to another.
During visits to several rural areas of Rajshahi, most authorised dealers were found without subsidised fertiliser, while nearby retail shops were selling the same products at significantly higher prices.
Under government-fixed rates, a 50kg bag of triple super phosphate (TSP) costs Tk1,350 and a bag of diammonium phosphate (DAP) Tk1,050. Farmers, however, said they were paying Tk1,700–1,800 for TSP and around Tk1,600 for DAP because of shortages at authorised outlets.
“I have a farmer’s card. I went to authorised dealers several times but could not buy fertiliser,” said Russel Hossain, a farmer from Baraikuri village in Paba upazila.
“Fertiliser is not available at the government-fixed price. But if you are willing to pay more, there is no shortage.”
At M/s Haque & Sons Enterprise, an authorised Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) dealer at Nowhata Bazar in Paba, no subsidised fertiliser was available during the visit.
Dealer Abdul Haque said he supplies fertiliser to several thousand farmers across 42 mouzas.
“In July, I received only 22 bags of TSP, 70 bags of MOP and 110 bags of DAP. The supplies were exhausted within two or three days,” he said.
An employee of Tasnim Enterprise, another authorised dealer, also said the shop’s fertiliser stock had run out. However, shop owner Fazlur Rahman later said fertiliser was available and claimed the employee had provided incorrect information.
At a nearby retail shop, an employee offered to sell a 50kg bag of DAP for Tk1,600, Tk550 above the government-fixed price. He said the shop collected fertiliser from various sources and claimed subsidised fertiliser passed through three or four middlemen before reaching retailers.
Farmers have long alleged that a syndicate involving dishonest dealers, unauthorised retailers and officials responsible for monitoring fertiliser distribution is controlling the market.
Several farmers, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that field-level agricultural officials were involved in the network. They also claimed that hundreds of unauthorised fertiliser retailers were operating as part of the system.
Sajedur Rahman, a farmer from Chhoto Palashi village in Rishikul Union of Tanore, said farmers could not find fertiliser at government-fixed prices.
“When we go to the dealers, they say there is no fertiliser. We are forced to buy from high-priced retail shops,” he said.
Farmers in Palashi said TSP was selling for Tk1,700–1,800 per bag, while DAP was available for around Tk1,600. MOP, officially priced at Tk1,050, was reportedly being sold for about Tk500 more.
Despite the allegations, officials said they had not received complaints about a fertiliser shortage.
Azizur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi division, said, “We have not received any complaints from farmers about a fertiliser shortage. Aman planting is underway everywhere, and agricultural officials are advising farmers.”
Kazi Shahidul Islam, Rajshahi district administrator and chairman of the district fertiliser distribution committee, said he had not received complaints about higher prices but promised to investigate.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, Rajshahi received higher allocations of TSP, DAP and MOP in July and August this year than during the same period in 2025.
The combined allocation rose from 5,876 tonnes in July 2025 to 7,033 tonnes in July 2026. August allocations also increased, with TSP rising from 1,430 tonnes to 1,511 tonnes, DAP from 2,404 tonnes to 2,647 tonnes and MOP from 1,709 tonnes to 1,760 tonnes.
Nasir Uddin, assistant director (fertiliser) at the BADC Rajshahi office, said the agency was distributing fertiliser according to the quantities approved by the Agriculture Ministry. He added that seasonal demand had increased because some farmers were applying fertiliser beyond recommended doses.
The Rajshahi agricultural region, comprising Rajshahi, Natore, Naogaon and Chapainawabganj, has set a target of cultivating Aman rice on 410,000 hectares. About 40% of the targeted area had been planted as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, farmers in Chapainawabganj’s Gomastapur upazila staged a protest on Wednesday after failing to obtain adequate fertiliser from dealers.
Farmers from Rahonpur Union gathered at the upazila parishad premises and later met Upazila Nirbahi Officer Zillur Rahman.
They said fertiliser was unavailable during a critical stage of Aman cultivation and warned that delays could reduce crop yields.
Gomastapur Upazila Agriculture Officer Saklain Hossain said officials were monitoring the supply situation and would take action if problems were found.
UNO Zillur Rahman said necessary measures were being taken to ensure farmers received fertiliser at government-fixed prices. He warned that legal action would be taken against anyone found selling fertiliser above the fixed price, hoarding supplies to create an artificial shortage, or harassing farmers.

Strong assurances received on renewal of Ganges Water Sharing Treaty
item.description:
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Water Resources was informed on Thursday that strong assurances have been received regarding the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, commonly known as the Farakka Treaty.
The committee was also informed that the main implementation work of the Teesta Master Plan is expected to begin next year.
The first meeting of the committee on the Ministry was held at the National Parliament with committee chairman Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon MP presiding.
The committee discussed various initiatives including advance preparaFtions to prevent river erosion and tree plantation programs.
The meeting was informed that the Padma Barrage Project has already been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
A presentation was made before the committee on the overall activities of the Ministry of Water Resources including ongoing development programs, project progress, implementation periods and allocations.
According to the presentation, 93 development projects are currently being implemented under the ministry. A total of Tk 7,832.80 crore has been allocated for these projects in the 2026-27 fiscal year.
The committee called for completing the development projects within their stipulated timelines, ensuring proper and efficient use of allocated funds and taking more effective measures to improve public services.
The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty was signed by Bangladesh and India on Dec 12, 1996 for 30 years and is due to expire in December 2026.
The treaty provides for sharing Ganges water at India’s Farakka Barrage during the dry season from Jan 1 to May 31 each year on the basis of a 10-day schedule.
Under the agreement, when the flow is 70,000 cusecs or less, Bangladesh and India receive 50 percent each. If the flow is between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs, Bangladesh receives 35,000 cusecs and India gets the remainder. When the flow is 75,000 cusecs or more, India receives 40,000 cusecs and Bangladesh gets the remainder.
With the treaty approaching expiry, its renewal has emerged as a key water-sharing issue between the two countries amid concerns over declining dry-season flows, climate change, rising water demand and downstream ecological impacts.

item.title: PM to attend ‘Rhidoye Dhaka 416’ event at Lalbagh Aug 29
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend “Rhidoye Dhaka 416,” the final event marking 416 years of historic Dhaka, at Lalbagh Fort in the capital on August 29.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Abdus Salam announced the details at a press conference at Nagar Bhaban on Thursday.
He said the 416th anniversary of historic Dhaka will be celebrated through a range of colorful programs highlighting the city’s rich history and culture.
The special celebration has been organized under the theme “Festival, Pride and Responsibility.”
“The event is being organized with the expectation of reviving Dhaka’s heritage. When people live with Dhaka in their hearts, they will also develop a sense of responsibility to keep the city clean,” Salam said.
He said various programs will be held at different locations across the capital until September 5 as part of the celebrations.
Final event at Lalbagh Fort
The final event will begin at 4pm on August 29 at Lalbagh Fort, the DSCC administrator said.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has kindly agreed to attend the event. The LGRD state minister and the administrator of Dhaka North City Corporation will also be present,” he said.
The event will feature dance performances by children, an exhibition of inventions by young scientists and an exhibition of books written about Dhaka.
There will also be stalls showcasing famous foods from Old Dhaka.
The prime minister will plant a tree and visit Lalbagh Fort during the event. He will inaugurate the program through the release of festoons and balloons, followed by the release of pigeons.
A traditional kite festival celebrating the heritage of Old Dhaka will also be inaugurated at the venue.
The special “Clean Dhaka, Green Dhaka” and mosquito-control campaigns will also be launched on the occasion and subsequently carried out in every ward, Salam said.
A documentary titled “Rhidoye Dhaka” will be screened at the event, while a commemorative book on Dhaka will also be unveiled.
The organizers also hope to unveil a commemorative postage stamp marking Dhaka Day, subject to approval from the relevant ministry.
The celebrations will conclude with a light-and-sound show and a cultural program after a short break, Salam said.

item.title: Four killed as bus collides with leguna in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
Four people were killed and five others injured after a bus collided head-on with a leguna (Mahindra) in Chakaria upazila of Cox’s Bazar on Thursday morning.
The accident occurred around 6:30am near the Baitul Mamur Jame Mosque area in Nayapara of Khutakhali Union on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway, said SI Mohammad Shamsuzzaman of Malumghat Highway Police Station.
The deceased were identified as Mohammad Jasim Uddin, of Segunbagicha village in Khutakhali; Mohammad Shahed, of Fulchhari Shiapara; Mohammad Rafique, of West Gajalia village in Eidgaon; and Mohammad Ziaul Haque, of Notun Office area in the same upazila.
Shahed, Rafique and Ziaul died while undergoing treatment at Cox’s Bazar District Sadar Hospital, while Jasim died at Malumghat Christian Memorial Hospital in the afternoon.
The injured are Syed Alam, his son Mohammad Sarwar, Ziaul Haque, Mohammad Delwar Hossain, and Syed Karim. They were taken to the two hospitals for treatment. Three of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.
According to police and local residents, a Lal Shobuj Paribahan bus was travelling to Cox’s Bazar from Noakhali Sadar, while the leguna was carrying passengers from Eidgaon to Chakaria. The vehicles collided head-on after reaching Nayapara in Khutakhali.
The impact left the leguna badly mangled. Locals rescued the injured and took them to nearby hospitals.
SI Shamsuzzaman said the accident occurred amid heavy rain early in the morning. Police later used a crane to remove the damaged vehicles from the highway, and traffic returned to normal about an hour later.
Police said legal procedures would be completed before the bodies are handed over to the victims’ families.

item.title: Govt moves to formulate policy on battery-run rickshaws
item.description:
The government has taken an initiative to formulate a policy for managing battery-operated rickshaws in city corporation, municipality, upazila and union parishad areas.
A discussion on the operation of three-wheeled low-speed battery-run rickshaws, commonly known as e-rickshaws, was held at the conference room of the Local Government Ministry at Bangladesh Secretariat here on Thursday.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam presided over the meeting.
The meeting discussed the measures to effectively manage the battery-run rickshaws in light of urban management, traffic discipline, road safety and existing realities. Representatives of relevant stakeholders also presented various opinions and recommendations.
Mir Shahe Alam said a policy for managing e-rickshaws is being formulated in accordance with the Local Government (City Corporation) Act, 2009 and the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act,20 26.
He said effective implementation of the policy would play an important role in controlling traffic congestion, maintaining traffic discipline and ensuring road safety in the cities.
The government authorities would generate revenue for the government exchequer.
The minister further said that, to achieve these objectives, steps would be taken to amend existing regulations and make them time-befitting with a view to establishing a coordinated licensing authority for city corporations, municipalities, upazilas and union councils.
It may be mentioned that relevant provisions and schedules of the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act, 2026 have already been amended to create scope for registering battery-operated rickshaws and issuing licenses to their drivers in city corporation areas.
Earlier, on December 14, 2025, the local government division issued the “Rules on the Operation of Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Operated Rickshaws (E-Rickshaws) in City Corporation areas, 2025” to regulate e-rickshaw operations in city corporation areas. The rules were published in the gazette on December 17, 2025.
At the meeting, Prof Dr Md Hadiuzzaman of the Department of Civil Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Burt) provided expert opinions on the issue.
Among others, Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator freedom fighter Md Abdus Salam, Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan, Local Government Division Secretary Md Shahidul Hasan, DNCC Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Asaduzzaman, DSCC Chief Executive Officer Md Khaibar Rahman and Additional Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Traffic) Md Anisur Rahman attended the meeting.
Senior officials from the ministry and the city corporations concerned were also present.

item.title: Speakers call for action to implement National Urban Policy 2025
item.description:
With more than one-third of Bangladesh’s population living in urban areas and cities contributing nearly 65% of GDP, speakers on Thursday called for coordinated action to implement the National Urban Policy 2025 and translate its commitments into more livable, inclusive and climate-resilient cities.
The call came at the National Dissemination Workshop on National Urban Policy 2025, jointly organized by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Local Government Division (LGD), with support from the UK government, at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre (BCFCC) in Dhaka.
The workshop aimed to disseminate the National Urban Policy 2025 among stakeholders and gather recommendations for drafting its implementation action plan.
The event brought together representatives from government ministries and agencies, local government institutions, development partners, academia, research institutions and the urban development community.
The government approved the country’s first National Urban Policy 2025 as a national framework for more planned, inclusive, sustainable and climate-resilient urban development.
Speaking at the workshop, Md Mahmud Ali, director (additional secretary) of the Urban Development Directorate, said urban development cannot be the responsibility of a single ministry and requires coordination across sectors, with active participation from ministries, public and private institutions, development authorities, academia, professionals and urban residents.
Md Samsul Islam, joint secretary of the Local Government Division, stressed that the next priority is to move from policy to implementation.
“We want the National Urban Policy 2025 to go beyond being a policy document and become an effective tool for real change in urban planning, management, infrastructure development and service delivery,” he said.
Tanvir Mahmud, senior governance specialist at UNDP Bangladesh, said implementation at the local level would ultimately determine the policy’s impact.
“The real success of the National Urban Policy will depend on how effectively it is applied in our cities. National policy directions need to connect with local realities, local capacities and local priorities,” he said.
He added that government ownership should remain at the centre of implementation, while development partners could support the process through technical knowledge, evidence, innovation, capacity development and partnerships.
The National Urban Policy 2025 was developed under the leadership of the Local Government Division, with contributions from an inter-ministerial committee and relevant government institutions, including the Public Works Department, Ministry of Planning, and Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. UNDP provided technical support with assistance from the UK government.
Earlier, Professor Dr Shakil Akther of the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology presented the National Urban Policy 2025, followed by an open discussion on its implementation.
Among others, Nathaniel Smith, team leader for climate and environment at the British High Commission; Amit Datta Roy, urban specialist at the Asian Development Bank; Dr Fawzia Farzana, professor at the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Khulna University; and Yugesh Pradhanang of UNDP spoke at the workshop.

item.title: Madrasa student’s death: Teacher placed on 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Thursday placed Hafiz Md Zakaria, 35, one of two teachers arrested over the death of a child student at Rowazatul Ulum Hafizia Nurani Madrasa in Rayerbagh’s Jorakhamba area, on a three-day remand.
The court did not hear the remand plea against Hafiz Md Zubayer Ahmed, 20, after his lawyer claimed he was a minor. The court fixed August 18 to hear the matter.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order on Thursday, said Abdus Sabur, a sub-inspector of the prosecution department.
After the hearing, relatives of the deceased allegedly attacked the accused as police were taking them to jail from the court premises.
The body of Naim Sheikh, 13, was recovered from a bathroom on the third floor of the madrasah around noon on August 3. His mother, Nazma Begum, later filed a case against the two teachers.
Police arrested the two accused from the madrasa around 10:00pm the same day. They were sent to jail the following day.
On August 5, Kadamtali thana Sub-Inspector Amzad Hossain, also the investigating officer in the case, sought five days’ remand for the accused. The court scheduled Thursday for the hearing in their presence.
During Thursday’s hearing, Advocate Harun ur Rashid Khan, appearing for the complainant, argued in favour of granting remand. Zakaria’s lawyer, Emdadul Alam, sought cancellation of the remand plea and bail for his client.
Zubayer’s lawyer claimed that he was a minor, prompting the court to defer the hearing on his remand.
The judge also sought Zakaria’s statement. He told the court that Naim went to the bathroom after the noon prayer call but did not return.
“Even after being called, he did not open the bathroom door. Senior students at the madrasah then opened the door and found him hanging by his shirt sleeve,” Zakaria said.
He said he was in Madanpur at the time and returned to the madrasa after receiving a phone call about the incident.
“When I arrived, his body was still warm. I called a doctor, who came and told us that the child was no longer alive,” he said.

Minister: Energy crisis to ease soon with FSRU repair
item.description:
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood on Thursday said that the country's ongoing energy crisis is expected to ease soon following the repair of a Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) and the arrival of LNG cargoes.
"The current gas shortage was triggered by an unexpected fire on an FSRU. While a major disaster was averted, the damage caused significant disruption to gas supplies and required specialized repairs by engineers from Britain and Singapore," he said.
The minister made the remarks as the chief guest at a discussion titled "Navigating Bangladesh's Energy Crisis: Immediate Priorities and the Path to a Sustainable Energy Future", organized by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) in the city.
Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said a 72-hour total shutdown would be required for boiler maintenance after completion of the second phase of repairs, which could temporarily worsen the gas crisis.
However, the government has already procured LNG cargoes, which will be unloaded immediately after the FSRU becomes operational, he said, expressing hope that the move would significantly improve the current gas supply situation.
The minister also highlighted a significant change in the country's electricity demand pattern, saying peak demand now extends beyond midnight and recently reached 18,000 megawatts. He attributed much of the night-time demand to the charging of battery-run rickshaws.
Many of the charging points use illegal electricity connections, he said, adding that the ministry faces public resistance and even physical altercations when attempting to disconnect such connections.
Outlining the government's long-term roadmap, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud said three new FSRUs would be established by 2029 at Payra, Mongla and Hiron Point to strengthen LNG supply and improve distribution, particularly in the Khulna region.
The government is also planning to construct an undersea gas pipeline from Chattogram to Bakhrabad to overcome limitations in the existing pipeline network, he said.
The minister said the government is taking steps to strengthen Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (BAPEX) after years of inadequate exploration, including ordering two new drilling rigs to intensify domestic gas exploration.
To provide immediate support to industries, he mentioned that the government has allowed a private company to transport gas from Bhola directly to factories.
He said Bangladesh is also holding discussions with Malaysia on introducing a containerized gas delivery system for industrial users, which could help supply gas without waiting for new pipelines to be constructed.
On energy-sector reforms, the minister said the government is moving away from the existing "single buyer system" to increase private-sector participation and strengthen energy security.
A new Fuel Oil Policy is being drafted to allow private-sector entities to import and distribute oil after consultations with stakeholders, he said.
Highlighting the recently adopted Solar Energy Policy, he said the government has introduced tax holidays and reduced duties on batteries and inverters to 5 percent to encourage the expansion of renewable energy.
Concluding his remarks, Iqbal Hasan Mahmood said the government is working on a war footing under the leadership of the prime minister to address the energy crisis and sought moral support from investors and the media in navigating the current challenges.

item.description:
Nomination papers must be submitted between 10am and 4pm on Thursday to run in the presidential election slated for August 20 next.
The ruling BNP has formally not declared its presidential candidate yet, while the opposition Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has named LDP Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed as its candidate.
However, both the ruling and opposition camps have collected nomination papers for their respective aspirants.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, who is serving as the returning officer of the presidential election, has already convened a meeting of the Members of Parliament (MPs) at the session chamber of the National Parliament on August 20 for voting in the presidential election in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission on August 06 last, the nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16 and the last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.
Voting will take place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm on August 20 in the session chamber of the National Parliament. A total of 349 MPs are voters in the presidential election. Now a parliamentary seat, Chittagong-4 constituency, remains vacant.
This will be the first presidential election in 35 years, which is going to involve more than one candidate. So, the voting is set to be held in the Presidential election after 1991.
The name of Local Government and Rural Development Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has already surfaced in the media as the BNP’s probable presidential candidate, but people are likely to wait till Thursday to formally know its candidate.
On July 24 last, Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned as President and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took charge as the acting president.
According to Article 123(2) of the Constitution, an election to fill the vacant office of the President must be held within 90 days of the post becoming vacant due to resignation.

item.title: Mango market buzzes in Chapainawabganj as season nears end
item.description:
Mango trading has gained momentum in Chapainawabganj as the season approaches its end, with large numbers of buyers and sellers gathering at major markets across the district.
At Kansat, the district’s largest mango market, trading of late-season and year-round varieties—including Ashwina, BARI-4, BARI-8, Gaurmati, Banana and Katimon—is continuing in full swing.
Thousands of maunds of mangoes are being traded at the market every day, while buyers and sellers remain active despite the season being in its final stage.
Speaking at Kansat market on Tuesday morning, mango grower Hasibul Hasan Babu of Binodpur union in Shibganj upazila said the season was almost over. He said he sold Ashwina mangoes for Tk 3,800 per maund that day, but the price was not satisfactory considering production costs.
Another grower, Monirul Islam of Durlabhpur union, sold BARI-4 mangoes for Tk 7,000 per maund. He said the variety used to fetch a much higher price several years ago. Although prices have improved somewhat recently, growers failed to receive their expected returns at the beginning of the season, he added.
Mango grower and media worker Farhad Ali brought Katimon mangoes to the market and sold them for Tk 6,000 per maund. While he was relatively satisfied with the price, he also expressed disappointment over the overall market situation this year.
Abdur Razzak, a trader involved in online mango trading for a long time, said prices had increased slightly toward the end of the season. However, the market remained unstable throughout the year. Traders like him still managed to make profits, he said.
Grower Abul Hasnat said Shibganj produces more mangoes than the district’s other four upazilas combined. He recalled that Fazli once accounted for nearly 80 percent of the orchards in the area.
In recent years, however, newer varieties such as Banana, Katimon, Amrapali and BARI-4 have increasingly entered the market around the time Fazli mangoes are harvested. As a result, demand for these newer varieties has risen during the late Fazli harvesting period, putting downward pressure on Fazli prices, he said.
Sentu Mia, a mango grower from the Maharajpur area of Sadar upazila, said he had been involved in mango cultivation for nearly two decades.
“Mango farming was profitable about 10 years ago, but growers have struggled to earn satisfactory returns in recent years,” he said. “Production costs have increased, but mango prices have not risen proportionately.”
Abu Taleb, president of the Shibganj Mango Aratdar Association, said the livelihoods of more than 100,000 people in Chapainawabganj were linked to the mango industry.
Production costs are rising every year, but growers are not receiving prices that adequately reflect those increases, he said.
He warned that the district’s mango industry is facing a serious threat and called for the development of mango processing industries, stronger agricultural research and the establishment of a full-fledged mango research institute to ensure the sector’s long-term sustainability.
Meanwhile, mangoes at Kansat, Rohanpur and other markets in the district are currently selling at around Tk 2,000-Tk 5,000 per maund for Ashwina, Tk 8,000-Tk 12,000 for BARI-4, Tk 5,000-Tk 7,000 for Gaurmati, Tk 5,000-Tk 8,000 for Katimon and Tk 12,000-Tk 15,000 for Banana varieties.
According to Atikul Islam, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Chapainawabganj, mangoes were cultivated on 37,487 hectares of land in the district this season, with a production target of 458,912 metric tonnes.
He said supplies of several varieties, including Ashwina, Gaurmati, Banana and BARI-4, were continuing even as the mango season entered its final stage.

Salman Shah family allegedly threatened after actor Don’s arrest
item.description:
The family of late actor Salman Shah has allegedly received death threats following the arrest of actor Ashraful Haque Don in the murder case involving the popular actor.
Mohammad Alamgir Kummkum, plaintiff in the case and Salman Shah’s maternal uncle, told reporters on Wednesday that Shahraan, Salman’s brother, had been threatened with death in a Facebook comment.
Kummkum showed journalists a screenshot of the alleged threat after appearing at a Dhaka court for Don’s bail hearing.
He said the threat was posted from a Facebook account named “Shakil Kibria” in the comments of a Facebook Live hosted by a Salman Shah fan named Mamun.
The screenshot showed the comment: “Mamun, tell Neela Chowdhury not to go too far regarding Salman’s death. Otherwise, we will kill Shahraan (Salman Shah’s brother) the way we killed Salman Shah.”
Kummkum said they would file a general diary (GD) with Ramna police over the threat, noting that the Salman Shah murder case was filed with the same police station.
Mamun, who was present at the court, said he was conducting the Facebook Live to call for a human chain by Salman Shah fans when the alleged threat appeared in the comments.
“The comment was later deleted while I was taking a screenshot,” he said.
“We, Salman fans, have been saying that he was murdered. Why are such threats coming after Don’s arrest? This should also be investigated,” Mamun said, urging authorities to bring everyone involved in the case to justice.
Don denied bail
Meanwhile, a Dhaka court rejected Don’s bail petition in the Salman Shah murder case.
On Wednesday afternoon, lawyers including M Faridul Islam and Tarikul Islam Jewel sought bail for Don before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ehsanul Islam.
Public Prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi opposed the petition, while the defence argued that there was no specific allegation against Don in the FIR or arrest warrant and that he was not involved in the alleged incident.
The court rejected the bail petition after hearing both sides.
Earlier, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) took Don into custody after receiving information from immigration authorities as he was preparing to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
He reportedly had a travel ban in connection with the Salman Shah murder case.
Murder case
Salman Shah died at his residence in Eskaton, Dhaka, on September 6, 1996. His death was initially recorded as a suicide, but a murder case was filed later.
The case has remained under investigation and legal scrutiny for decades.
On October 20, 2025, Kummkum filed a murder case with Ramna police on behalf of Salman’s mother, Neela Chowdhury, against 11 people.
The accused are Samira Haque, her mother Latifa Haque Lucy, businessman Aziz Mohammad Bhai, actor Ashraful Haque Don, David, Javed, Faruk, Ruby, Abdus Sattar, Saju and Rezvi Ahmed alias Farhad.
The latest death-threat allegation has renewed attention on the case, with Salman’s family and fans calling for an investigation to identify the person behind the threat and determine whether they have any connection to the murder case.

item.title: Bomb wrapped in pressure cooker recovered in Savar, defused
item.description:
Police recovered a bomb wrapped in a pressure cooker with scotch tape from a field in Savar’s Sadhapur area early Wednesday and later it was safely defused by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) bomb disposal unit.
Police and locals said the suspicious object was found inside a blue plastic drum at Ghora Mosque field around 1:30am.
The drum also contained some cloths and a copy of the Quran.
Savar Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Imran Hossain said they initially suspected that the object could be a bomb.
Locals removed the pressure cooker from the drum, placed it in the field and informed police.
Some residents said three unidentified people left the drum at the mosque field at night.
No one has been arrested in this connection yet.
A bomb disposal unit of DMP was informed and its members worked for about four hours before safely defusing the bomb in the afternoon, said the SI.
Earlier on July 30, police recovered another bomb concealed in a pressure cooker from an abandoned bag in front of Joyee General Store in Khejurbagan area of Ashulia.
The bomb disposal unit later defused it through a controlled explosion at a safe location.
Meanwhile, police on Tuesday night detained a youth named Arif Hossain with five crude bombs during a raid in Shyampur area of Hemayetpur in Savar.

item.title: Five arrested over Pallabi shooting linked to Tk15 lakh drug money dispute
item.description:
Five people, including a notorious drug trader, have been arrested in connection with a shooting incident in the capital’s Pallabi area over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
The arrestees are Hamid Khan alias Makhon, drug trader "Lengra" Rubel, Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa, Parvez and Rabbi.
Police recovered a foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets, two magazines, 1,000 Yaba pills and two vehicles allegedly used in drug trading from their possession.
Additional Commissioner (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
He said the shooting took place in front of Emon’s tea stall at Mirpur Section-11 under Pallabi police station around 5:30pm on Aug 7.
Alamgir was shot in the abdomen and head, while a female passerby named Josna sustained a gunshot injury to her leg, he said.
Following a complaint filed by Alamgir’s wife, a case was filed with Pallabi Police Station on charges of attempted murder.
The DB Mirpur Division subsequently launched a shadow investigation.
With the help of video footage and information technology, investigators identified a Toyota Premio car used in the shooting and arrested its registered owner, Hamid Khan alias Makhon, from Pallabi.
During interrogation, Makhon told investigators that although the car was registered in his name, its actual owner is notorious drug trader "Lengra" Rubel.
Based on his information, Rubel’s associates Parvez and Rabbi were arrested from the Kalshi area.
Later, acting on information provided by Parvez and Rabbi, detectives arrested Lengra Rubel and Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa in an area beside the embankment near Eastern Housing under Rupnagar Police Station.
A foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets and two magazines were recovered from them.
During preliminary interrogation, the arrestees said the shooting occurred following a dispute between Alamgir and Lengra Rubel and his associates over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
DB officials said Alamgir himself is a listed drug trader and faces several cases in Dhaka, but he is the victim in this case.
Responding to a question, Shafiqul Islam said anyone involved in a crime would be identified as a criminal regardless of their other identity and brought under the law.
He said Rubel faces several cases and investigators are looking into whether he invested money earned from drug trading in different places. If necessary, information will be sent to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for possible action under the Money Laundering Prevention Act.
The DB chief said preliminary interrogation also revealed that several other people, including Bappa, were in the vehicle during the shooting. Their identities are not being disclosed for the sake of investigation, and efforts are underway to arrest them.
Apart from the attempted murder case, separate cases under the Arms Act and Narcotics Control Act are being processed.
The arrestees may be taken on remand for further interrogation, while DB operations to arrest others involved in the incident are continuing, Shafiqul said.

Dhaka records ‘moderate’ air quality Wednesday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 34th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 71 at 9:35am.
According to the AQI scale, the capital’s air quality was classified as ‘Moderate’, indicating that it generally poses little or no risk to the general population, though unusually sensitive individuals may experience some health concerns.
Malaysia’s Kuching topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 223, followed by Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo with 179 and Baghdad in Iraq with 176.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while 151 to 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is categorized as ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Gunmen fire at 11-storey building overTk50L extortion demand in Ctg
item.description:
Gunmen fired two shots at the gate of an 11-storey building owned by an expatriate businessman in Chittagong Hamzarbagh area on Monday night, allegedly after a Tk50 lakh extortion demand went unmet.
The incident took place around 11pm, sparking panic among residents.
The building, Runa Tower, is owned by Mohammad Yusuf, whose two sons are expatriate businessmen. Their ancestral home is in Fatikchhari. Yusuf is the father-in-law of Azizur Rahman Aziz, general secretary of the Chittagong city unit of the banned Awami League-affiliated Swechchhasebak League. Aziz was arrested two days after the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024, and remains in jail.
Building security guard Mohammad Alamgir Hossain said there was no electricity at the time.
“Two young men wearing pants and shirts suddenly arrived and asked us to close the gate. They then fired two shots at the gate before walking away. Hearing the gunshots, local residents gathered, and police later arrived,” he said.
Yusuf said his son Shawkat received a voice message on WhatsApp from a foreign number around noon on Monday, giving him one hour to pay Tk50 lakh.
According to Yusuf, the message claimed the senders knew where his children lived and worked and had details about their properties. They threatened to kill them if the money was not paid within the stipulated time.
Panchlaish police station Officer-in-Charge Jahedul Islam said gunmen fired at the building gate after the extortion demand was not met.
“We are working to identify and arrest those involved. No case has been filed yet,” he said.
The incident comes amid a series of alleged extortion-related attacks in Chittagong.
On July 13, associates of alleged criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon were accused of attacking and vandalising a businessman’s under-construction building in the Bor Dighirpar area of South Pahartali Ward after he allegedly refused to pay Tk20 lakh in extortion. A case was filed over the incident, followed by a demand for Tk50 lakh.
Earlier, on June 13, Emon’s associates were also accused of attacking and vandalising internet service provider DDN on Bakalia Access Road over an alleged demand for Tk2 crore.
Following the incidents, locals held human chains and press conferences demanding an end to extortion and Emon’s arrest.
Emon allegedly became increasingly involved in extortion and other criminal activities after August 5, 2024. He was arrested in Jessore on July 29 while allegedly attempting to flee to India and is currently on a 10-day remand.

item.title: Fishing resumes in Kaptai Lake after 3.5-month ban
item.description:
Fishing has resumed in Kaptai Lake after a three-and-a-half-month ban, bringing fishermen, traders and transport workers back to the lake and its busy landing centres.
The ban on fishing, fish transportation and marketing ended at midnight on Monday. From early Tuesday, motorised boats began arriving at the Kaptai fish landing centre with catches from different parts of the lake, including Bagaichhari, Langadu, Barkal and Bilaichhari.
The first boats reached the centre around 6:30am, carrying drums filled with kachki, chapila, tengra, ayir, baim, bacha, kaligunia and pabda.
The landing centre quickly became busy as fishermen unloaded their catches and traders prepared the fish for shipment. After paying the required duties, traders packed the fish in ice and loaded them onto trucks bound for Chattogram, Dhaka and northern districts.
A total of 28,866kg of fish were landed at the Kaptai centre between 6:30am and 1pm on Tuesday, said Jasim Uddin, head of the Kaptai Fisheries Development Sub-centre. The government collected Tk6.20 lakh in revenue from the day's catch.
At Rangamati Fisheries Ghat, traders said the first day's catch was dominated by smaller fish.
Md Shahjahan said adverse weather on Monday had prevented many fishermen from casting their nets, making it too early to assess the season's overall catch.
“Fish are generally smaller at the beginning of the season. Larger fish are usually caught later,” he said.
Commander Mohammad Foyez Al Karim, manager of the Kaptai Lake Fisheries Development and Marketing Centre, said a substantial quantity of fish had reached the landing centre by noon.
He said traders might be concerned about the relatively small size of chapila but expected the fish to grow larger within the next 10 to 15 days.
Foyez said the fish production target for the 2025-26 fiscal year was 8,500 tonnes, but actual production reached 10,000 tonnes, generating Tk22.60 crore in revenue.
The district administration initially imposed this year's fishing ban from April 25 to July 31 to allow fish to breed and replenish stocks. The ban was later extended by 10 days until midnight on August 10.
The reopening has brought relief to thousands of people whose livelihoods depend on the lake, while traders, transport workers and others are expecting increased economic activity.
Kaptai Lake, Bangladesh's largest artificial reservoir, is a major source of fish and hydropower and an important water transport and tourism route. Its resources are closely linked to the economy and livelihoods of people across Rangamati.

item.title: Dhaka-Gopalganj train service starts
item.description:
For Gopalganj residents who have waited years for a direct train to the capital, marked the end of a long journey — but the new service has arrived with a catch: its evening schedule.
The Abhijatri Commuter made its first trip from Dhaka to Gopalganj on Monday, opening a direct rail link between the district and the capital through the Padma Bridge rail route.
The train left Kamalapur Railway Station at 3:30pm and reached Gopalganj at 7:10pm. After a brief reception at Gopalganj Railway Station, it departed for Dhaka at 8:05pm.
The service will run six days a week, except Saturday, with 609 seats. The fare from Gopalganj to Dhaka has been set at Tk145, while the journey takes around three and a half hours.
Under the regular schedule, the train will leave Dhaka at 3:30pm and reach Gopalganj at 6:45pm. It will leave Gopalganj at 7:15pm and reach Dhaka around 10:30pm, stopping at nine stations.
The launch drew crowds to Gopalganj Railway Station, where residents gathered to witness a rail connection they had been waiting years for.
For many, the low-cost service is expected to ease travel to Dhaka for education, healthcare, business and employment. But passengers say the evening schedule limits its usefulness, particularly for students, traders and women.
Md Zakir Hossain of Khatia Garh Union in Gopalganj Sadar travelled to Dhaka with his wife on the inaugural train.
“We are extremely happy and excited that train service from Gopalganj to Dhaka has finally started after such a long wait,” he said.
But he urged the authorities to introduce a morning service.
“This is not just my demand; it is the long-standing expectation of the people of Gopalganj,” Hossain said.
Shabnur Khanom, a third-year honours student at Gopalganj Government College, said the train would significantly reduce travel costs for students.
“We often have to travel to Dhaka for job examinations and other purposes. A bus journey costs around Tk500, while the train fare is only Tk145,” she said.
She said a morning service would allow students to reach Dhaka earlier and reduce the risk of missing examinations because of traffic congestion.
For fish trader Motaleb Fakir, the timing is an even bigger concern.
“If the train left Gopalganj around 7am, we could take fish and other fresh produce to Dhaka and return the same day,” he said, adding that an evening service could force traders to stay overnight in Dhaka and incur additional costs.
Gopalganj Railway Station Master Ratna Baidya said the 609-seat service would operate six days a week and provide an affordable travel option for people heading to Dhaka.
The railway project connecting Gopalganj was taken up in 2010. The Rajbari-Gopalganj-Tungipara railway line was inaugurated in November 2018 after construction and renovation work costing around Tk2,110 crore.
Despite the railway infrastructure, Gopalganj had no direct passenger train to Dhaka.
That changed after the Dhaka-Bhanga railway line opened in December 2024 under the Padma Bridge Rail Link Project, creating the opportunity for a direct connection.
With Monday’s launch of the Abhijatri Commuter, Gopalganj has finally gained that long-awaited link — though passengers are already asking for a timetable that works better for them.

item.title: Jute cultivation exceeds target in Khulna region
item.description:
Jute cultivation in Khulna agricultural region has exceeded the seasonal target, with favourable weather, higher prices and growing demand for eco-friendly products encouraging farmers to expand the crop.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), farmers in Khulna, Bagerhat, Narail and Satkhira have cultivated jute on 38,361 hectares this year, surpassing the target of 38,287 hectares.
With the peak harvesting season now underway, farmers across the region are busy harvesting jute, while canals, beels, rivers and ponds have turned into busy sites for retting, fibre extraction and drying.
So far, farmers have harvested jute from 20,083 hectares, producing around 90,535 tonnes of fibre — about 51.9% of the region’s cultivated area.
During a recent visit to Terokhada upazila in Khulna, hundreds of men and women were seen working along the Atharobeki River and nearby beels in Baoisona and Kolabaria villages.
Women’s participation in post-harvest processing was particularly noticeable. Many women separate fibre from retted jute without entering the water, often taking jute sticks instead of cash as payment.
“I extract jute fibre in exchange for keeping the jute sticks,” said Jharna Begum of Kolabaria.
Tohura Banu, a first-year student at Terokhada College, said she helps her family process jute during college holidays.
“I enjoy the work, and it also helps my family,” she said.
Mahmud Gazi, who was working in the Atharobeki River, said a team of 15 labourers earns around Tk800 a day, while some workers are paid Tk5 per bundle.
Across the region, freshly extracted fibres can be seen drying on bamboo frames, bridge railings and around homesteads, while piles of jute sticks line village roads.
Farmers said favourable rainfall has made retting easier this year.
Mahtab Hossain of Baoisona village, who cultivated jute on three bighas, said heavy rainfall during Ashar and Sraban filled nearby water bodies, reducing the cost of transporting jute to retting sites.
However, frequent rain and limited sunshine have made drying the fibre difficult, he said.
Jute is also proving useful in maintaining the productivity of farmland between major crop seasons.
Soumen Bairagi of Golna village in Dumuria said farmers can grow jute between the wheat or pulse harvest and Aman rice cultivation, preventing land from remaining fallow.
“Early sowing in Chaitra also allows farmers to harvest jute in time for Aman transplantation,” he said.
Farmers also cited better prices and expanding domestic and international markets as key reasons behind the renewed interest in jute.
Trading of the new season’s jute has already begun at major markets in Khulna, including Khalishpur, Daulatpur and Khanjahan Ali.
Farmer Anser Ali said he sold freshly harvested jute for Tk3,700 per maund at Daulatpur market.
Veteran jute trader Fazlu Sharif, former vice-president of the Bangladesh Jute Association, said he expected prices to remain profitable for farmers and traders.
Jute is currently selling for Tk3,500-Tk4,500 per maund, with prices expected to rise further as marketing gains momentum.
Md Rafiqul Islam, additional director of the Khulna Agriculture Region, said average production currently stands at around 8.5 maunds per bigha and is expected to increase as harvesting continues.
“Abundant rainfall this season created favourable conditions for jute retting,” he said.
He attributed the rise in cultivation partly to increasing global demand for environmentally friendly products, saying higher prices have encouraged farmers to expand the crop.
The government has also provided incentives, while the agriculture department is supporting farmers through training and modern production technologies, he added.

item.title: Home minister urges US businesses to boost investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Tuesday urged US businesses to increase investment in Bangladesh, assuring them of a business-friendly environment and comprehensive security for foreign investors.
The minister made the call when a high-level delegation from the US-Bangladesh Business Council (USBBC), led by its President and US Chamber of Commerce Senior Vice President for South Asia Atul Keshap, met with him at the conference room of the Home Ministry at the Bangladesh Secretariat this afternoon.
During the meeting, they discussed various issues of bilateral interest, including ways to increase bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and the United States, as well as energy and security cooperation, according to a ministry press release.
The minister reiterated the government's strong commitment to creating an investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh and ensuring overall security for foreign investors.
He said Bangladesh currently offers ample opportunities for foreign direct investment (FDI), while the government has ensured a tariff-friendly environment for the convenience of investors.
Welcoming increased US investment in Bangladesh, the minister said the government has taken necessary legal and administrative measures to launch a one-stop service called "Invest Bangladesh" to bring the investment process under one umbrella and make operations easier.
He said administrative and legal facilities in this regard have been streamlined over the past five to six months.
The government is also examining various proposals for setting up LNG terminals at strategically important locations in the country, which would help diversify the energy sector and enhance overall national security, he said.
The minister further said major opportunities are being created for investment in food grain and energy supply, ranging from government-to-government (G2G) arrangements to private-sector investment.
He said initiatives have also been taken to introduce digital security measures, the "Safe City" project under smart policing, "Integrated Border Management" for border security and e-visa facilities to strengthen national security and technological protection.
Atul Keshap said major US companies have been successfully operating in Bangladesh for several decades and are currently among the country's major investors.
Highlighting Bangladesh's immense potential, he said the country's economy is expected to reach $1 trillion by 2034.
To achieve this target, he said, developing technical and managerial capacity, along with increasing GDP growth and tax productivity, is crucial.
He also discussed how US companies could provide comprehensive support and become partners of the Bangladesh government in the country's development process.
A 16-member delegation of business leaders from the US-Bangladesh Business Council, led by Atul Keshap, and senior officials of the Home Ministry attended the meeting.

item.title: JU English dept holds workshop on visual thinking, literary theory
item.description:
The Department of English at Jahangirnagar University (JU) held a workshop on visual thinking and idea generation on August 2, introducing MA students to creative approaches to understanding and applying contemporary literary and cultural theories.
Titled “Visual Thinking and Idea Generation,” the workshop was held from 11:30am to 1pm at the department as part of the MA course LECS 502: Contemporary Critical Theories and Pedagogies (Critical Humanities).
Cartoonist and illustrator Eeha Nawar attended the session as the guest speaker.
The four-credit core course introduces students to a range of theoretical frameworks, including Affect Theory, Ethical Criticism, Trauma and Testimonial Criticism, Medical Humanities, Posthumanism, Ecocriticism, Cognitive Literary Criticism and Digital Humanities.
During the workshop, Nawar demonstrated how visual arts, media texts and editorial cartoons can be used alongside literary theories to explore contemporary cultural and social issues.
She said literary theory was not confined to written texts and discussed how visual thinking could offer alternative ways of approaching complex theoretical concepts.
“Learn, study and understand the other side of the story. It helps develop critical thinking and contributes to building a strong character,” Nawar said.
Students participating in the workshop explored different methods of visualising ideas through art, including mind mapping, selecting visual elements and developing concepts across different media.
The session also covered the use of digital installations, graphic texts, cartoons and doodles as tools for developing and communicating ideas.
The workshop concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, during which students discussed ways of applying visual media and digital humanities approaches to their course materials.
Other students from the department also attended the session.

item.title: Chief Whip: MPs bound by party line in presidential election
item.description:
Chief Whip of Parliament Nurul Islam Moni on Tuesday said members of parliament will not be able to vote in the presidential election, slated for August 20, against their party's decision as Article 70 of the Constitution remains unchanged.
“As Article 70 of the Constitution has not been amended, it will remain effective. No one will be able to vote beyond the party's decision. If anyone does so, their membership of Parliament will be cancelled,” he said at a press briefing at the Media Centre of Parliament after the 2026 presidential election preparatory meeting held at the Cabinet Room of Parliament.
Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal chaired the preparatory meeting. Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Whips Md G K Gouse, Rakibul Islam Bakul, Mia Nuruddin Ahmed Apu, Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia and A B M Ashraf Uddin Nizan also attended the meeting.
Speaking at the meeting, Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal said the state structure must be freed from fascism in all spheres.
“The 2026 presidential election is going to be held at a historic moment in building a fascism-free Bangladesh,” he said.
During the meeting, all necessary preparations, including the use of the Jatiya Sangsad chamber for holding the 2026 presidential election, all necessary logistical support and ensuring the attendance of Members of Parliament, were discussed.
The meeting also instructed completing all necessary preparations and providing logistical support for the election.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission, the 2026 presidential election will be held in the Parliament chamber on Thursday, August 20.
The Chief Election Commissioner will conduct the election as the return officer in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991. EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, Parliament Secretary Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan and other senior officials concerned of the Parliament Secretariat were present at the meeting.
At the press conference, Chief Whip Nurul Islam said the BNP's candidate for the presidential election has not yet been finalised. “The party has entrusted the Prime Minister with the responsibility of finalising the candidate. He will announce the candidate,” he said.
He said the opposition has already nominated a candidate and the meeting was held to ensure a fair election.
“According to the election schedule, voting will be held in the Parliament chamber from 2pm to 5pm on August 20,” he said. Nurul Islam said the voting will take place inside Parliament and a ballot box will be placed there. Members of Parliament will cast their votes according to their division and seat number, he added.
He said preparations would be made to declare the result before the scheduled closing time if all 349 votes are cast within the first hour of voting. If it is found that one vote remains, it will wait until 5pm. After 5pm, the result will be announced, he said. The Chief Whip said the voting of the (Acting) President, Leader of the House, Leader of the Opposition and (Acting) Speaker would be broadcast live. After voting is completed, the counting of votes and the process leading to the declaration of the result may also be broadcast live, he said.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said the presidential election should have been held in accordance with the “July Charter” to intensify acceptance and dignity of an elected president.
As the election was being held anyway, the opposition did not want to allow it to take place without a contest, he said.
